To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the δ13C values and the negative δ18O-δ13C relationship are both sensitive to the seasonality and strength of the summer monsoon precipitation in northern China.

(1) the negative δ18O/δ13C relationship in pedogenic carbonate is caused by the seasonality of monsoon precipitation; (2) the spatial patterns of C3/C3 biomass in East Asia are closely related to the seasonality and intensity of summer monsoon precipitation; and (3) the seasonality of precipitation may be a key factor in determining the response of C3 and/or C4 plants to climate change in East Asia.

the δ13C–δ18O relationship of pedogenic calcium carbonate from northern China provides a new proxy to evaluate the strength of the Asian summer monsoon, and that a stronger summer monsoon during MIS 5 led to a northward shift of C3 forest vegetation in the southern Chinese Loess Plateau, while a stronger summer monsoons during MIS 7 and the Holocene did not lead to a significant northward displacement of forest vegetation.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the spatial distribution of pedogenic carbonate in the Loess Plateau is a sensitive indicator for the strength of the summer monsoon, and the isotopic values of the carbonate nodular are a good record of the seasonal distribution of monsoon precipitation.
a narrowly-focused summer monsoon precipitation favors C4 plants while a scattered summer monsoon precipitation supports the growth of C3 plants.
